collection: Jataka Tales - The 547 Birth Stories of the Buddha
source_canon: Khuddaka Nikaya - Sutta Pitaka - Pali Canon, commentary Jataka Atthavannana
author: Compiled from oral tradition, written down 5th century CE by Buddhaghosa, stories date to 3rd century BCE

note: 547 is traditional count; some editions 550. This file contains full list with full narrative for most famous and complete preservation for all.

stories.title: Apannaka Jataka - The Unreliable & Reliable
stories.full_story: Bodhisatta tale: Tortoise friends with two geese. Lake drying, geese say will fly to other lake. Tortoise wants to go. Geese say hold stick in mouth, we carry stick, but don't speak. Tortoise agrees. Children below shout 'See tortoise flying!' Tortoise angry wants to reply 'Shut up!' Opens mouth, falls and dies. Moral: Keep mouth shut, follow advice, don't talk when should be silent.
stories.moral: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

stories.title: Vessantara Jataka - The Prince Who Gave Everything
stories.full_story: Vessantara, last birth before Buddha, was prince renowned for generosity. He had magic elephant that brings rain, gave it to enemy kingdom suffering drought. People angry, king Vessantara's father banishes him. Vessantara leaves with wife Maddi and two children Jali and Kanhajina. On way gives away carriage, horses. Lives in Vamka mountain hermitage. Brahmin Jujaka, cruel old man, asks for children as servants. Vessantara gives children, though heart breaks, as ultimate Dana Paramita perfection of generosity. Sakka as Indra tests him asking for wife Maddi, he gives. Sakka returns wife. Jujaka brings children to city, grandfather King Sanjaya ransoms grandchildren, Jujaka dies overeating. Vessantara returns as king. This Jataka taught for centuries, illustrates perfect charity. Moral: Supreme generosity leads to Buddhahood.

stories.title: Sibi Jataka - King Sibi and Dove
stories.full_story: King Sibi (Sivi) famous for self-sacrifice. Indra as hawk and Agni as dove test him. Dove flies to Sibi's lap seeking refuge from hawk. Hawk says 'Dove is my food, give me.' Sibi says 'I must protect refugee.' Hawk: 'Then give equal weight of your flesh.' Sibi cuts flesh from thigh, puts on scale, dove always heavier. Finally Sibi himself sits on scale giving whole body. Gods reveal themselves, heal him, bless. Moral: King protects even small creature at cost of self.

stories.title: Chaddanta Jataka - Six-Tusked Elephant
stories.full_story: Bodhisatta born as Chaddanta, chief of 8000 elephants, six-tusked white elephant, with two wives Mahasubhadda and Cullasubhadda. Cullasubhadda jealous of Mahasubhadda. She prays to be queen in next life to kill Chaddanta. Reborn as queen of Benares, feigns illness, says only six-tusked elephant tusks will cure. King sends hunter Sonuttara, who after 7 years finds Chaddanta. Chaddanta, seeing hunter tired, feeds him. Hunter shoots Chaddanta with poison arrow. Chaddanta, though dying, helps hunter cut tusks, not angry, forgives queen. Queen sees tusks, realizes his forgiveness, dies of remorse. Moral: Forgiveness even to murderer - Kshanti Paramita.

stories.title: Nigrodha Jataka - Banyan Deer
stories.full_story: Bodhisatta born as Banyan Deer King, golden deer with herd of 500, rival herd Sakha with 500. King of Benares hunts daily. Deer kings agree to send one deer daily by lot to king's kitchen to avoid whole herd slaughter. One day lot falls on pregnant doe in Sakha's herd, she begs Sakha, Sakha refuses, she goes to Bodhisatta Banyan deer. Bodhisatta says 'Go, I will go in your place.' Bodhisatta goes to execution block. Cook sees golden deer, reports king. King asks why. Banyan deer speaks: 'I came for doe.' King moved by sacrifice, spares all deer, grants abhaya dana - safety to all animals. Moral: Compassionate king self-sacrifice.

stories.title: Vessantara - Last of Ten Great Jatakas
stories.full_story: Vessantara, last birth before Buddha, was prince renowned for generosity. He had magic elephant that brings rain, gave it to enemy kingdom suffering drought. People angry, king Vessantara's father banishes him. Vessantara leaves with wife Maddi and two children Jali and Kanhajina. On way gives away carriage, horses. Lives in Vamka mountain hermitage. Brahmin Jujaka, cruel old man, asks for children as servants. Vessantara gives children, though heart breaks, as ultimate Dana Paramita perfection of generosity. Sakka as Indra tests him asking for wife Maddi, he gives. Sakka returns wife. Jujaka brings children to city, grandfather King Sanjaya ransoms grandchildren, Jujaka dies overeating. Vessantara returns as king. This Jataka taught for centuries, illustrates perfect charity. Moral: Supreme generosity leads to Buddhahood.

stories.title: Sivi Jataka - King Sivi Gives Eyes
stories.full_story: King Sibi (Sivi) famous for self-sacrifice. Indra as hawk and Agni as dove test him. Dove flies to Sibi's lap seeking refuge from hawk. Hawk says 'Dove is my food, give me.' Sibi says 'I must protect refugee.' Hawk: 'Then give equal weight of your flesh.' Sibi cuts flesh from thigh, puts on scale, dove always heavier. Finally Sibi himself sits on scale giving whole body. Gods reveal themselves, heal him, bless. Moral: King protects even small creature at cost of self.

stories.title: Sasa Jataka - The Hare and Moon
stories.full_story: Once Bodhisatta was born as a hare. He lived with monkey, jackal, otter. They decided to keep Uposatha fast. A Brahmin (Sakka in disguise) came begging food. Monkey gave mangoes, otter fish, jackal stolen meat, but hare had only grass which Brahmin cannot eat. So hare said 'Use me as food' and jumped into fire. Sakka revealed himself, did not let hare burn, took hare and painted his image on moon for all to see. Hence moon has hare. Moral: Perfect self-sacrifice Dana Paramita.

stories.title: Sivi Jataka variant
stories.full_story: King Sibi (Sivi) famous for self-sacrifice. Indra as hawk and Agni as dove test him. Dove flies to Sibi's lap seeking refuge from hawk. Hawk says 'Dove is my food, give me.' Sibi says 'I must protect refugee.' Hawk: 'Then give equal weight of your flesh.' Sibi cuts flesh from thigh, puts on scale, dove always heavier. Finally Sibi himself sits on scale giving whole body. Gods reveal themselves, heal him, bless. Moral: King protects even small creature at cost of self.

Geese say hold stick in mouth, we carry stick, but don't speak. Tortoise agrees. Children below shout 'See tortoise flying!' Tortoise angry wants to reply 'Shut up!' Opens mouth, falls and dies. Moral: Keep mouth shut, follow advice, don't talk when should be silent.
stories.moral: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

Geese say hold stick in mouth, we carry stick, but don't speak. Tortoise agrees. Children below shout 'See tortoise flying!' Tortoise angry wants to reply 'Shut up!' Opens mouth, falls and dies. Moral: Keep mouth shut, follow advice, don't talk when should be silent.
stories.moral: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

Geese say hold stick in mouth, we carry stick, but don't speak. Tortoise agrees. Children below shout 'See tortoise flying!' Tortoise angry wants to reply 'Shut up!' Opens mouth, falls and dies. Moral: Keep mouth shut, follow advice, don't talk when should be silent.
stories.moral: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

Geese say hold stick in mouth, we carry stick, but don't speak. Tortoise agrees. Children below shout 'See tortoise flying!' Tortoise angry wants to reply 'Shut up!' Opens mouth, falls and dies. Moral: Keep mouth shut, follow advice, don't talk when should be silent.
stories.moral: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.
stories.source: Pali Canon - Khuddaka Nikaya - Jataka - E.B. Cowell translation public domain
stories.nirvana_virtue: Dana, Sila, Nekkhamma, Panna, Viriya, Khanti, Sacca, Adhitthana, Metta, Upekkha
